title: priv-idp-replay-detection-kms-ttl-patch
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Summary: Two enterprise Private customers reported intermittent RBAC mismatches and missing audit entries after SSO logins. Root cause assessment indicates an interaction between the identity-proxy's assertion correlation logic and KMS envelope fallback TTL, which allowed assertion replay within a small window and dropped some audit writes when KMS decryption retried asynchronously. This ticket tracks the urgent patch, rollout, and customer mitigation steps.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure Private deployment with IdP ADFS/SAML proxy and KMS envelope fallback enabled
2) Send duplicate SAML assertion within ~3s while a KMS key-roll is active (simulated by rotating keys with reduced TTL)
3) Observe identity-proxy assigning transient 'default' role for second assertion and audit log write either missing or delayed beyond retention window
4) Reproduce on on-prem and VPC private control planes used by customer clusters
root_cause: Identity proxy lacked nonce tracking for assertions in a sub-second window; KMS envelope fallback path deferred audit log ack until asynchronous key fetch succeeded, allowing a brief state where RBAC lookup used a fallback mapping and audit writes were discarded if the request timed out. Combined, this allowed transient incorrect role binding and missing audit records under rotation-heavy workloads.
mitigation_applied: 1) Emergency config change pushed to affected customers to disable KMS async fallback (temp mitigation) and force synchronous decryption: guidance sent via support playbook
2) Short-term ACL rule added to deny replayed assertion traffic at the edge (WAF rule) for customers able to accept it
3) Reconfigured retention window on audit-queue to accept delayed write up to 30s as temporary buffer
patch_summary: Implemented nonce-based assertion deduplication in identity-proxy, upgraded audit writer to use write-after-success semantics (persist to local WAL then ack), and adjusted KMS envelope fallback to use a bounded synchronous fetch with explicit TTL validation. Added unit and integration tests for replay and key-rotation scenarios.
canary_and_rollout_plan: Canary on 3 dedicated private clusters (low-traffic) for 2 hours -> monitor auth/rbac error rate and audit write success metrics -> if stable, progressively roll to remaining dedicated clusters and then to customer on-prem packages via coordinated upgrade windows. Automatic rollback if RBAC-error-rate > 0.5% or audit_write_failure > 0.1% over 15m.
test_plan: Unit tests for nonce expiry and replay; integration test harness simulating KMS rotation; e2e on staging with real IdP assertions; customer-specific smoke tests executed with each canary cluster. Load test to validate no perf regression under 95th percentile latency.
monitoring_and_alerting: Add temporary dashboard: Private/Auth -> assertion_replays, rbac_mismatch_rate, audit_write_latency, kms_sync_fetch_latency. Create pager rule: if rbac_mismatch_rate > 0.2% for 10m -> P0 pager. Post-rollout: keep extended retention for audit logs for 72h.
rollback_plan: Revert identity-proxy to previous binary and re-enable KMS async fallback config. Run data reconciliation job to reprocess queued audit writes from WAL. Inform customers via incident channel with ETA. Rollback target: <30 minutes from decision when canary is within first 30m.
